item.title: Trump ordered to testify in $10bn BBC lawsuit discovery: What happens now?
item.description:
A federal judge on Thursday ordered President Trump to sit for a deposition by Dec. 11 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC over an edit of one of his speeches that the president's lawyers say was misleading. Why it matters: The order will likely force Trump to answer questions under oath in a legal battle he started. Driving the news: Judge Enjoliqué Lett ordered Trump to appear by Dec. 11, after lawyers for the BBC argued that Trump is improperly delaying his appearance. In a filing published Wednesday, Trump's counsel said the president could appear between Jan. 11 and Jan. 22, 2027, and argued that his presidential duties prevent him from sitting for the deposition before then. They also allege the BBC is "wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action." The president was originally scheduled to appear for the deposition on Oct. 16.…

item.title: Rep. Ilhan Omar says she will move out of her Washington, DC, home after federal search
item.description:
Embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) said she’s planning to vacate her Washington, D.C., home, claiming that a number of threats have made her feel like remaining there would be unsafe. Omar made the declaration in her first televised interview since federal law enforcement agents executed a search warrant at that home, taking a number of electronic devices and documents related to the ongoing investigation into the congresswoman’s citizenship status. “Obviously, I can’t continue to live there,” Omar told MS Now host Chris Hayes. “So we have to figure out where to move to because our address has been public, and with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids visiting off and on, having people track them.” CHECK OUT THE DAILY WIRE MIDTERM HUB Omar, who has repeatedly insisted that she has done nothing wrong, ignored the fact…

item.title: Russia strikes Kyiv hours after agreeing to US-brokered peace talks – video
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told White House envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday that he "agrees in principle" resuming trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. to end the war, according to Russian and U.S. officials. Why it matters: The White House hopes Putin will show more willingness to compromise after President Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian diesel sales and took other steps welcomed by Moscow. For now, it seems the only concession Putin agreed to is to negotiate. Driving the news: During a three-hour meeting in St. Petersburg, Witkoff presented Putin with an updated proposal to end the war in Ukraine . Trump envoy Jared Kushner joined virtually.
